title: Multidisciplinary, biopsychosocial factors contributing to return to running and running related stress urinary incontinence in postpartum women
authors: Moore IS, James ML, Brockwell E, Perkins J, Jones AL, Donnelly GM
population: 881 postpartum women who completed an online questionnaire on running experience
findings: Median time to first postpartum run was 12 weeks.

Higher odds of returning to running: running during pregnancy (OR 2.81, 1.90-4.15), high weekly volume (OR 1.79, 1.22-2.63), lower fear of movement (OR 0.53 per unit, 0.43-0.64) and no vaginal heaviness (OR 0.52 for heaviness, 0.35-0.76).

Risk factors for running-related stress urinary incontinence (SUI): having returned to running (OR 2.70), SUI before pregnancy (OR 4.01) and during pregnancy (OR 4.49); caesarean delivery lowered odds (OR 0.39).
Authors suggest fear of movement, vaginal heaviness and running-related SUI before or during pregnancy be addressed early by healthcare providers.
limitations: Self-selected online survey with retrospective self-report; associations only, no outcome-based timeline of safe return.
implications: Ask about pre-pregnancy and pregnancy SUI, vaginal heaviness and fear of movement at postpartum onboarding and route positive answers to pelvic health care.
The 12-week median is descriptive of what happened, not a recommended return date; do not set a default return date from it.

verification.notes: Added by verifier. Crossref (BJSM, 2021-06, first author Moore) matches; ORs confirmed in the Europe PMC abstract (PMID 34144950). Odds ratio directions for return-to-running as stated in the abstract (OR 0.52 attached to 'not suffering heaviness').
